name: The Family and the Fishing Pole
objectiveText: Catch 6 Darkshore Grouper for Gubber Blump in Auberdine. Darkshore Grouper  ( 6 )

comments.body:
Why was this harder for me to figure out than some other skills? Just an idiot, I guess.

Anyway, if you do the quest, Gubber will lend you a pole. If not, you need to buy one (fishing trainer and supplies in Darnassus and Lakeshire), the bait (shiny bauble to start) and get trained.

Find a body of water, equip the pole (replace your main hand weapon with the pole), "bait" the pole (with the bauble or better bait), then (I didn't realize this was necessary) find the Fishing icon in your spellbook and drag it to an icon bar. Click on the fishing icon and you will cast. You'll see the green fishing "progress" bar on your screen. You need to recast when the progress bar disappears. Just keep recasting until you get the fish you want.

When the bobber moves and you put the cursor over it, you get a gear icon. Right-click the gear icon and you will get a fish, something else or the message that "your fish got away" (same thing as an empty loot box). I left the cursor on the icon most of the time but you don't need to do that.

I did the Bubber Glump quest and got to lvl 14 in about 18 minutes, with the 6 required fish and about 8 others. XP was only 100 but after all, my 54 Druid was late to the game.

Why start now? Look up Deviate Fish and you'll understand. I stole the recipe from the Gadget AH. Why not? Everyone should be a fisherman.
replies: For those playing Classic: Go into the building with Thundris Windweaver. Jump overthe railing behind him onto the rock. Fish north, and in 3 minutes, 12 casts, I had the 6 fish needed. I expect they spawn like any other animal target, and if you fish near other players, it takes 18 minutes instead of 3.

A very easy quest. Gubber Blump will even lend you a fishing pole for the task. You can start fishing directly next to Bubber Blump. The quest can easily be completed with a very low fishing skill.

There are a few fish that you can pull in. Oily Blackmouth can normally be sold in the auction house for quite a few silver each.

The quest should take less than fifteen minutes and will also raise you fishing skill while your doing it.

replies: You don't have to have a lot of skill to pull unlocked chests full of items from the water. What you do need is to keep your eye open for "oil slicks" and "floating wreckage." I was pulling chests before I barely had any skill at all. Oil slicks tend to give you easily unlocked chests with mats for leatherworking, tailoring or smithing, along with fish that alchemists are willing to pay big bucks for at AH. Floating wreckage can give you all this plus bloated fish that usually carry gems, locked boxes, and, the more skill you have, Mithril Lockboxes. I'm currently an artisan. Fishing pays for

In case anyone has not figured out how to catch the fish, place your cursor over the bobber and click when you see the bobber move.  That's how you catch the fish.

To use the fishing pole, make the fishing pole your primary weapon. To cast, click on the fishing pole icon.  Also, make sure you buy some of the bait stuff that Blump sells.

Ron.

Just talk to Gubber who gives you the quest. Tell him you don't know how to fish and he can teach you. He can also sell you a fishing pole. The reward fishing pole is nice, but you can also sometimes find a +5 pole for sale on fishing supply vendors (worth getting when you see it if you like to fish).
